question.knowledge_point: Finding the Divergence of a Vector Field in Two Dimensions
question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F=x\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,i+y\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,j.$ 
Evaluate $∇\cdot F$ at the point $(3,4).$
question.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field on ${R}^{2}$ and the partial derivatives of the components of $F$ all exist, then the divergence of $F$ is the scalar field given by

$$
∇\cdot F=\text{div}\,F=\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}.
$$

  

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y} \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(y\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}+\frac{{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{2}+3{y}^{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}} \\  & =3\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate $\text{div}\,F$ at the point $(3,4),$ and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(∇\cdot F)(3,4) & =3\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =3\sqrt{9+16} \\  & =3\sqrt{25} \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$
